commits: 432dba3a Send the wizard to two-factor enrollment after requiring it
708ea568 Merge remote-tracking branch origin/dev into docs/747-suite-verification

ranges.otherFiles: Every other changed path is under docs/ (DOC-029 evidence and article edits), not application code.
ranges.change: In applyAuthentication, after the wizard saves a legal policy with requireTwoFactor on, it now navigates to /auth/two-factor/enroll instead of /welcome. Before, the /welcome navigation did not rerun the loader guard, so the Administrator was not sent to enrollment. welcome.test.tsx adds a test for the new route. No API, worker, message, Settings page, enroll page or session guard code changed.

method: For the 45 records on 3fa407e3 I relied on their round 2 compatibility evidence for 3fa407e3 to 57e77e38 and reviewed 57e77e38 to 432dba3a on top. For the 10 records on 57e77e38 I reviewed 57e77e38 to 432dba3a. I read every article that touches the wizard, sign-in, two-factor authentication or Authentication settings. I grepped all articles for two-factor, enroll, wizard and welcome. Only first-run describes the wizard Authentication step. For configure-analysis I reviewed the full 3fa407e3 to 432dba3a diff on the AI provider path.
limitations: Source review only. I ran no walkthrough and used no lab or provider account.
first-run is out of scope for this review.

In apps/web, settings-ai-analysis.tsx changed only the Provider card intro text, which the article does not quote, and moved the key reuse check into lib/ai-connector-config.ts as canReuseAiKey. I compared the old and new code. Both require hasApiKey, the same preset and protocol, a saved base URL, and equal normalized base URLs, so the rule in Disable, rotate, or remove is unchanged. The live provider check on 3fa407e3 (V-C43, walkthrough-c43.json) used a real OpenRouter connector with deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash. It covered Test connection success, Load models, search and refresh with 444 models, Field prompt save, line break, restore and reset, an automatic Analysis run and a deliberate rerun with Version, model, evidence and Unverified values, the evidence panel, the no-primary-Document refusal, turning the connector off and on, the Legal Team Member view, and a Load models refusal from a missing Custom endpoint path. On 57e77e38 round 2 (walkthrough-r2-1.json) re-ran 18 credential-free steps and all passed: page and card order, presets and forms, save refusals, API refusals, Load models against a closed endpoint, a fictional Custom connector with a failing test, the turned-off state, the changed-destination key rule, Field prompts, the Contracts to Fields link, Remove connector, the Legal Team Member refusal, the signed-out help link, and operator checks of the shared OPENLAW_SECRET_KEY and key-free logs. It could not re-run the live provider steps. Those steps run only code that did not change, so I judge the article compatible. The article contentSha256 a2e55ab5 still matches its evidence. Known issue #887 remains and the article still makes no Escape claim.
